title: Collaboration: Deduplicate Notifications and Respect Preferences
businessContext: A reconnect replay sends the same mention notification repeatedly, including muted channels and messages the recipient wrote.
problemStatement: Implement solution({ recipientId, mutedChannels, mentionsOnly, events }). Events are valid { id, authorId, channelId, mentionIds } with nonempty string IDs and arrays of string mentionIds. Process in arrival order. An already-seen event id => duplicate; first occurrences consume the ID even if suppressed. Then authorId==recipientId => self; muted channel => muted; mentionsOnly without recipient in mentionIds => skipped; otherwise delivered. Return { delivered: [event IDs], outcomes }. A replay with changed contents still uses the first event decision. No actual delivery is performed.
constraints: Implement the synchronous solution(input) contract exactly. Do not mutate input; all inputs are JSON data.
This is a deterministic state model. It does not open sockets, send notifications, authorize real users, or establish media connections.
candidateTasks: Reproduce the starter failure, implement the invariant, and pass every authored case.
How would an outbox and provider idempotency key handle a crash after sending but before recording success?

testCases.name: Suppressed ID remains consumed on changed replay
Empty event batch produces no notifications

hints: Write down validation and replay precedence before changing state.
Use stable IDs and monotonic sequence/version values; preserve input ownership.
alternativeApproaches: Use an append-only event log with transactional projections.
Use a database snapshot plus a versioned resume cursor.
commonMistakes: Trusting delivery order or treating retries as new operations.
Mutating caller-owned arrays or accepting cross-channel data.
Presenting a fixture result as a guarantee of real-time delivery or media connectivity.
